content: Ligand 2 is a charged fused aminal with SA 4.64; ligand 1 a hydantoin sulfone, inactive. Atom 0 on ligand 1 is a terminal methyl over an acyclic bond, so I keep that carbon and discard the other 27. The open lead from the last run is the azine C4 position, which I had wrongly written off as substituent-insensitive and which turned out to span 0.49 for a methyl up to 0.60 for a bromine - still climbing when the budget ended. What I do not know is what it is reading. Bromine and nitrile both score at the top but have almost nothing in common electronically: bromine is large and polarisable and only weakly withdrawing, the nitrile is small and strongly withdrawing. A methylthio separates them. It is about the size of a bromine and even more polarisable, but it donates electron density rather than withdrawing it. If polarisability is what matters, this should land near 0.60; if electron withdrawal is, it should fall back toward the methyl. The surviving methyl becomes the S-methyl, which is why this host suits the question. Expected product: about 299 Da.
